chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:
"If she gives birth to a child after six months, he belongs to the latter [husband], and if it is less than six months, he belongs to the first [husband]."
ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined for a child born to a woman after she has been married to two different husbands?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *luhq* (attribution) in cases of *iddah* overlap, where a woman marries a second husband before her waiting period from the first ends. It sets the six-month threshold as the minimum for a valid pregnancy, thereby determining whether the child belongs to the first or second husband based on the duration of gestation relative to the marriage timeline.
